utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor. Would you please stand and read aloud the affirmation on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Could the Chamber mention to counsel for all parties that we are conscious that we have been slipping behind in recent days, and in the case of this witness, we have, of course, a detailed written report, and we would hope, because of that, that counsel for all parties avoids going over material that is already covered adequately in the report, so that we can focus on matters additional to the report or which are thought to be controversial in the report. Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Professor Taseva.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, we have met already, but I will still introduce myself. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I appear for the Defence of Mr. Ljube Boskoski. I kindly ask you, Ms. Taseva, would you state your full name before this Court.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: My name is Slagjana Taseva.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, you and I do not speak the same language, but you do understand very well the language that I am speaking, and I do understand the language that you are speaking. That would give us an opportunity to swiftly exchange questions and answers. However, my question and your answer need to be interpreted for the Chamber and the colleagues in the courtroom to be able to understand what I'm asking and what are you answering. Therefore, I ask you to wait a while, to pause after my question until the question is interpreted and reply only after that. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, I will ask you questions that are derived from your report. I am clear that your report contains your opinion on several specific issues. I will still ask you in order to further clarify the process through which you arrived at a certain conclusion or an opinion, to elucidate on the way and process of your producing the report, and the factual basis you had in mind when you were giving your opinions or conclusions. Before we move on to those questions, I will kindly ask that the first binder is distributed to the witness and the Chamber, and the first document in it is the CV of this expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, in case I have misunderstood you or you misunderstood me, the CV of the witness, for example, has been clearly set out in the papers. It shouldn't need you to go to it unless there is some particular omission or matter that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understood you fully. However, I would like just to indicate several of the professional achievements of Madam Taseva, and I would like Ms. Taseva to confirm before this Court that that is her CV so that I could tender it into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Certainly the last part is fine. I suspect that we would disagree about the first part, but your intentions are not altogether clear to me yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe I would be able to clarify. When we offered this report, the Prosecutor requested in addition to the CV, some additional information that the Defence provided in the response to the Prosecutor's motion with regards to the expert opinion. Perhaps it would be proper to repeat this part only, because it is not fully contained in this CV. If the Court believes that this is part of the response that we gave to Prosecutor's motion, then it won't be necessary to go over this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will, no doubt, remember that you were successful in respect of that motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I received the response that I needed and I will not go over that again. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, we have here your CV, that is 65 ter 1D1277 in our list of exhibits. Tell me, Madam Taseva, is everything that is written in this CV the accurate and truthful description of your academic professional and other achievements and activities that you were involved in and that you are still performing?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Absolutely and fully, everything is truthful and correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, after this answer, I seek to tender the CV of Professor Taseva as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, could you clarify for us what was the subject of your expert opinion and what was the process through which you produced the report that we are discussing before this Honourable Court?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The topic of my expert report were a number of issues posed by the Defence which pertain, for the most part, to the procedures in the legal system of the Republic of Macedonia, to the legal positioning of institutions and their place and role in undertaking specific activities related to police activity and penal procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of your report, which is 65 ter 1D1279, 1D0225, enumerated are the issues that the Defence raised with you and asked you to respond to them in accordance with the -- your expert knowledge and professional experience. Tell me, Professor Taseva, were those all questions that the Defence asked you so that you produce your expert report on the basis of those?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is exactly so. On page 3 of the report, in point 1, the topics are listed about which the Defence asked of me to provide my expert report. If there is need, I will read through them. I will read these topics. This is the position of the Ministry of Interior within the structure of the Republic of Macedonia. Then division of labour, or relationships within the Ministry of the Interior. Employees of the Ministry of Interior. The concept of authorised official. Role and position of the minister in the Ministry of Interior. Functioning of the chain of command of the Ministry of Interior. Role and function of the employees of the Ministry of Interior in relation to criminal investigations. The role of the minister of interior and criminal investigations. The role of the minister of interior and disciplinary process. Special commissions in the Ministry of Interior. And the Law on Amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor Taseva. Considering the fact that this is the very beginning, we read through the materials to an extent but we will follow the instructions of the Chamber and in the further course of the examination, I will take into account and I kindly ask to you take into account that we do not need to repeat what has already been stated in the report. Professor Taseva, tell me, please, before the Defence requested you to produce the report on the issues that we mentioned, did you ever have contact with the team of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. At the onset of 2006 - I believe it was the end of February or the beginning of March, I cannot recall the exact date - was my first meeting with Mr. Dragan Godzo and with you. During this time we talked about whether I would accept to provide an expert position on another report which the Defence had from another expert. This was our first cooperation, the beginning of 2006. Once this report was completed and submitted, the ensuing meeting was at the end of 2006, in September. I believe September 2007; I cannot exactly remember the dates, at which time you asked of me to prepare this report. In the meantime, there were other contacts because previously we agreed that if you -- you required my opinion as a consultant on certain issues, that you should feel free to turn to me. As a result, we had several contacts from the beginning of 2006 till today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That first contact, Madam Professor, tell me whether it was about your opinion as a consultant to the findings of Terry Burgess, that was the report that -- or the expert that the Prosecutor's office offered as an expert on police matters.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the questions that the Defence gave you and asked you to answer to them through your opinion and findings, tell me whether the Defence gave you any materials that would be of importance and assist you in producing your report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Once I began preparing the report on the topics which I read previously, the Defence made available to me certain documents, on the basis of which it was possible to make the assessment about the functioning of the system and the procedures in the Republic of Macedonia in practice. However, also parts of statements of some of the witnesses here as part of this process.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, when did you complete your findings and when did you submit those to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Since I would say this is quite voluminous work, I submitted it somewhat late. At the beginning of this year. Later, once I handed over the report I was asked to amend it with certain facts and data which is introduced in the footnotes; that is to say, the material used and the previous statements of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood what you said well, you submitted one report to the Defence towards the beginning or middle of January, but later, you also produced the amended report which contained the footnotes. Tell me, Professor, what are the contents of those footnotes? Which documents or which grounds that you indicated and what was the purpose that they were serving?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The footnotes list the regulations, the law and the constitution in Macedonia which I used in preparing my expert opinion. Other by-laws which I also used in preparing this expert opinion, as well as references of certain documents which were made available to me by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you submitted the amended report to the Defence, did you then indicate to the Defence that there was any other problem with regards to your report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This was a technical mistake, I would say, in the report, because regarding the competencies of the Ministry of the Interior, twice the same contact was copied unnecessary and superfluous. I pointed out that this was a mistake and I asked that this be stricken out from the report or that a note be made that this is a mistake and other technical mistakes and errors. Two or three related to the English language.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you are mentioning the English language, tell me, Professor Taseva, do you speak any foreign languages?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the others, I speak and I write the -- in the English language.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which was the language in which you composed your report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I composed the report directly in the English language because I wanted to avoid translation problems of some very specific terminology.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to everything you stated, could you confirm before this Court that this report that we have after your CV and bears the number 65 ter 1D1279 is indeed the report that you produced and which reflects your opinion of the issues asked of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This document is the report that I prepared, and it contains my viewpoints and opinions about the issues that were asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this moment I seek to tender the expert report of Professor Slagjana Taseva, Ph.D., into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, I would ask you several questions with regards to your relation with the Defence team, the Defence of Mr. Boskoski. Tell me, first of all, are you acquainted with Mr. Boskoski and have you met him?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're not acquainted with him?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: We do not know each other personally and we have not met each other before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart your relation to the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski, in relation to your provision of expert opinion as a consultant with regards to the second expert opinion and also in relation to the request that you produce your expert report dealing with the issues of interest for the Defence, tell me whether you or any member of your family has any relation with the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. My daughter, Viktorija Taseva, works as a legal assistant in the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your selection as the expert for this case have any influence with the issue of selection of your daughter Viktorija as a part of the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No, there was no influence. This was a matter of circumstance, I would say. Because I had been in contact with the Defence since 2006 when Viktorija was still a student in Great Britain and later when she returned from her studies in September 2006, we learned that the Defence was looking for a legal assistant, and further contacts were established independently of me. She established direct contact with members of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this fact, your daughter Viktorija being part of the team of Defence of Mr. Boskoski, could it have or has it had any influence over your decision to accept this task or did it have any impact on your objectivity employed when you were establishing your facts and expressing your own opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. This had no influence over my decision to accept the cooperation with the Boskoski team for further preparation of a new report, nor could that have or influenced my position presented in this report in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor Taseva. And now I will move to some questions that are related to your report. I will kindly ask you to look now at page 6 of your report. That is 1D310. Page is 1D0228. Do you see it now? Do you see that page, Professor Taseva?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the report on page 6 in paragraph 14 you indicated that, pursuant to the Constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, the president of the republic is the commander in chief of the Armed Forces. I'm interested to hear, Professor, with regards to this constitutional position of the president, to whom is the president authorised to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In regards to the constitutional position of the president of the Republic as the supreme commander of the armed forces, the president has the competence to issue orders to the army and to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This president's function, is it further stipulated in any other laws?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This role of the president is further stipulated and elaborated in the Law of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning item 14, we have the footnote number 15 relating to that item. In order to clarify how you came about your conclusions, please tell us what this footnote actually represents.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: As one can read, this footnote represents and states that the sentence to which footnote -- this footnote refers specifies that this assertion is claimed on the Article 79 of the Constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, where it is expressly stated that the president is the supreme commander of the armed forces. And also the footnote lists transcripts, number of transcripts, which were made available to me by the Defence which also confirm my position by presenting how this actually functions in practice, because this is a transcript of statements of persons who are professionals.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, since you mentioned the Law on Defence, tell me whether the Law on Defence can limit or abolish this constitutional right on the part of the president of the Republic?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Of course that it cannot. The laws implement the basic constitutional provisions and principles. Therefore, the constitution is higher legal act than the law and the law cannot change the meaning of the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your report you also state that during the time you studied - that is 2001 - that there were some changes to the Law on Defence. Can you tell us anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. In the analysis of the documents which I made in preparing this report, it became evident that in the middle of 2001, that is to say, on the 1st July, 2001, a new Law on Defence was enacted, a law which, in accordance with the rules in the Republic of Macedonia, came in -- or comes into force eight days after its publishing in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia. That is to say, on the 8th of July that same year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why is it important that you mentioned the existence of both the old and the new law? Was there a need of sorts for you to clarify that, and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I felt that it should be clarified, the fact that in the meantime a new Law on the Defence was passed because the provisions which are incorporated in the new Law on Defence introduced changes in the competencies of the president related to the implementation of his function as supreme commander in terms of the use of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the analysis you carried out of the documents you had at your disposal, this new provision of the new law, was it actually put in place, was it implemented, and if the answer is negative, can you explain what the legal impact of it was?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In the last provisions of the new law, which, in our legal system, have the name of transitional and final provisions but also in some other provisions of this law, it is listed that a large number of by-laws have to be passed which will facilitate the operationalisation and implementation of the law in practice. For some of these by-laws the legislature provides a term of one year while for other there is a two-year deadline for passing these by-laws. However, the transitional and final provisions clearly state that up until the day of the passing of the new by-laws, the existing ones are implemented, adopted on the basis of the previous Law on Defence, unless these are contrary to the law. In this case, since this is not the case, since they're not contrary to the law, the by-laws which were adopted on the basis of the previous Law on Defence remained in force for a longer period of time in 2001 and 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, in keeping with those transitional and final regulations during 2001, was the position of the president of the republic in relation of use of police forces changed or did it remain the same as it was in the old law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: At that time, in the course of 2001, the position of the president of the state remained as established by the old law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having in mind the new provision contained in the provisional and final regulation, did you base your opinion and your finding on some other documents you used when preparing the report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. In preparing the report, I had -- I had insight of some documents which were prepared at that time of changing of the law - that is to say, in June 2001 - where one could clearly see that even after the passing of the new law, the president of the state continued to practice his authority deriving from the previous law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification, Your Honour, the witness has testified that while preparing her report in the English translation said: "I had insight of some documents which were prepared at the time of the changing of the law - that is to say, in June 2001." And if -- perhaps counsel could just clarify: Are these documents contained in the footnotes of the report and are they in the possession of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will try to clarify this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, concerning the issue you have just addressed, you noted your opinion in item 18, which is page 7 of your report, which is 1D0229, in that item, you refer to four footnotes. You heard my learned friend's request for clarification. Tell us whether those four footnotes contain the documents you studied and served as the basis of your opinion that you just stated before this Chamber as well as using them in writing your report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, those were the documents and sources you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this clarifies the situation sufficiently. I believe the Prosecutor is in possession of all these exhibits and documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that meet your concern, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, do you know whether the by-laws you mention in your findings, which can be also found in the transitional final provisions of the new law, were in force in 2000 and 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. The by-laws which we're talking about were not passed in 2001 and 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor Taseva, we come to page 7. I want to direct your attention to paragraph 17 of your report, whereby you mention joint operations of the army and police forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. We have here the matter of joint operations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, under whose competence was it to order joint operations of the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Joint operations of the army and the police can be ordered by the supreme commander of the armed forces, and this is the president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding such operations, what could the president decide on, in such circumstances? And what was your conclusion, based on the overall material you had studied, which was used as the basis of your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: On the basis of the constitution, on the basis of the Law on Defence, on the basis of the materials which I had available, I could conclude that the president could have and used these legal and constitutional authorisations to determine the situation in which the joint forces of the army and the police should act, the scope, the volume and the manner in which they will act, and also to establish who will lead with that situation or with that specific action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, in such situations, what is the position of the police forces participating in joint operations? Under whose command are they?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Regularly in situations such as these, the joint operations are commanded by members of the army, that is to say, the armed forces, while the police is always in the role which is subordinate to that of the army. In situations such as these, the role of command is in the hands of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Law on Defence that you mentioned, the both of them, we have the principles of controlling the army fully stipulated. We had the notions of the single chain of command, the unity of command and so on and so forth. Professor Taseva, do you know whether any other state body bases its activities on such principles, the principles of command I mentioned, including subordination as exercised by the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No, no other body in the Republic of Macedonia does not act nor is it structured in the way in which the army of the Republic of Macedonia is. No other body in the Republic of Macedonia does not act and is not positioned in the single chain and unity of command principle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 18, the word -- the "army" of the Republic of Macedonia was interpreted as the "armed forces" of the Republic of Macedonia. Therefore, I'd kindly ask that that be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although your previous answer is the answer to my next question, since you said that no other state body functions and is organised in that way, I'm particularly interested to know whether the Ministry of the Interior functions along the same principles of organisation as the army does?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. The Ministry of Interior does not function along the same principles. They do not have the principle of singleness of command and unity of command. This principle does not exist in the Ministry of Interior. This is a principle of the army but not of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the basic way in which members of the Ministry of the Interior perform their tasks?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Unlike the army, which functions on the principle of command and on the principle of orders, the Ministry of Interior is a body which functions on the principle of laws and implementation of legal competencies of the Ministry of Interior by each individual employed in the Ministry of Interior, in accordance with the competencies of that one individual, on the workplace where he is employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Professor Taseva, in item 7 of page 7, in item 29 of page 10, and in items 76 and 77 of page 19 of your report, you briefly and in general terms provide your opinion regarding the administration of security and counter-intelligence. First of all, please have a look at item 7 at page 7. It is 1D0029 -- I apologise. Item 7 is page 5, actually; I apologise. You mention the administration for security and counter-intelligence as being under the supervision of the parliament. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. In item 7 on page 5, it is listed that in charge of supervising the performance and work of the counter-intelligence section is the parliamentary commission which is to say the parliament, the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At page 10, item 29 of 1D0232, you, again, mention the administration for security and counter-intelligence as one of two independent bodies within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The administration for security and counter-intelligence and the administration for public security are the two autonomous bodies within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At page 19, paragraphs 76 and 77 of 1D0241, again, you provide your opinion -- or, rather, your conclusion as to what the administration for security and counter-intelligence is.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, concerning this body which is a part of the ministry, tell us a few other things, please. First of all, tell us what the competences of the administration for security and counter-intelligence are?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The competencies of the UBK, the administration for security and counter-intelligence, are noted in the Law on Internal Affairs. Specifically, the competencies of this administration within the ministry are: Counter-intelligence activities; activities for uncovering and preventing of threats against the institutions as determined in the constitution of the Republic; activities also of suppression of forms of crime which have elements from abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us show Exhibit P86 to the witness, please. It is the Law on Internal Affairs, Article 13 of the law at page N000-8984 in the Macedonian; and N000-8965 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your previous answer, you said that the competencies of the administration for security and counter-intelligence are stipulated by the Law on Internal Affairs. Do you base your opinion on the provisions referred to here; namely, Article 13 of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, my opinion is based on Article 13 of the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2 of the Article it says: "Protection against espionage, terrorism or other activities directed towards tearing down the democratic institutions as established in the Constitution of the Republic of Macedonia with forceful means, as well as protection from serious forms of crime." A while back you said that these were serious criminal acts which were related with elements from abroad. Can you please tell us whether these serious forms to which this provision refers to, are they regulated with the criminal procedure and law in Macedonia, and, if so, can you tell us how and under what title are these matters dealt with, the criminal legislation in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The protection from more serious forms of crime which contain within elements of trans-national crime, international elements is one of the competency of the administration for security and counter-intelligence. And this type of crime belongs to the type of organised crime, as well as money laundering and crimes aimed at tearing down the democratic institutions determined in the constitution in the Republic of Macedonia and terrorism. They can be found in many chapters and many provisions in the criminal law of the Republic of Macedonia. They're not concentrated in one chapter or one provision of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the penal code of the Republic of Macedonia, are such crimes envisaged which go against the protection of state order and are the authorities and competencies of the administration stipulated therein?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. There are such criminal offences or incriminations - espionage, the incrimination terrorism - which are criminal activities for the detection and suppression of which the directorate for security and counter-intelligence is involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the administration for security and counter-intelligence, as a body of the ministry, have -- has at its disposal specific rules and methods that it can use in order to exercise the competencies and authorities it has been entrusted with?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. The directorate for security and counter-intelligence has at its disposal specific methods and means which it uses to exercise its competences. A part of those methods and means are the special investigation methods such as surveillance, but there are also other means and methods that are used and that are the exclusive, specific means used by the directorate and there are some combined measures involving undercover agents, also penetration into the crime scene that is investigated, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How are such means used? Or, rather, to what extent the -- are they linked to any activities of the UVK --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, UBK. Could the counsel please repeat the end of her question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The administration for security and counter-intelligence, can it use those specific methods for any other activities of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The specific means and methods used by the directorate for security and counter-intelligence could not be used within the other part of the remit of the Ministry of the Interior. So they are separate and they are intended to be used exclusively within the activities and work within the competencies of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, and those are not the measures that could be used in order to detect other types of criminal activities, those that are processed by other parts of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, you will probably agree that one of such specific methods could also be tapping, wire-tapping of telephone conversations of the enemy or other persons which may perform certain acts directed at undermining the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this area regulated, and could one use such methods when it comes to one's own citizens or members of its own forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In principle, when these means are used by the directorate or the bureau for security and counter-intelligence, they are directed towards, I would call them foreign elements that are active on the territory of Republic of Macedonia and their application for another purpose would be illegal, I would say, since they could be used only in specific cases when specific prerequisites are met. In order to use a measure of this kind by the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, it is necessary to have and to respect certain procedure within which the need of use of such measure needs to be well elaborated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, is there any relevance of this issue in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm referring to a number of questions posed by Mr. Saxon of certain Defence witnesses. Therefore, I wanted to clarify with this witness, if possible. I don't have the exact transcript pages. In any case, the questions had to do with the use of the administration for security or rather the possibility to use that administration in order to investigate some other events or occurrences which fall outside the remit of the administration. That is the only reason why I asked the professor to clarify for us whether that is possible and under what circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see I have prompted Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Not exactly, Your Honour. I was tempted to rise to my feet before your intervention. My concern is actually something a bit different from the Chamber's concern. It's simply that I don't believe the information given in the last response or two by the witness is provided within the text of her expert report. And so if -- if the Defence is going to rely on this testimony, the Prosecution would at least like to know specifically what laws or other sources the witness relies upon in drawing these conclusions so that we can try to study them ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to mention the page I referred to in my previous question. It is page 9020, line 25, witness Igno Stojkov. However, I can move on concerning the report drafted by professor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon made the point that it is unclear whether you're seeking to rely on some aspect of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning witness Vesna Dorevska, what was admitted was the rules on the work of the state security directorate. Therefore, it is one of the exhibits in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I just think it might be more helpful for the witness to tell us what she relies upon rather than the Defence counsel speaking for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For what proposition, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if this is an expert witness giving expert evidence, the Prosecution would just like to hear from the witness what is the basis by which she came to this expert conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm still searching for what it is that is relevant in this case in this line of questioning. And if that's identified, then there might be content to your concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My questions, Your Honour, and their relevance, had to do with the questions posed to Mr. Stojkov by the Prosecutor. He was asked: Did you ever ask for assistance of the UBK of the Ministry of the Interior in identifying a useful piece of information which would have to do with the events in Ljuboten. It is page 9021, or, rather, the last line on 9020 and the first two lines of 9021 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Right. And then what is the relevance of the evidence that has just been given to that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Professor can answer, the relevance would be whether the directorate for state security, according to her knowledge, is, first of all, authorised; and secondly, does it have means at its disposal in order to address the issues which have to do some other crime-related procedures which the crime police of the Ministry of Interior is originally tasked with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer given by Mr. Stojkov to the question was no; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojkov said that the working group he was a part of did not raise such issues. As to whether the directorate for state security can be used in that regard is something that remains open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you see my concern? He was asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He said no, and the matter was left there. Now there is no issue whether -- if he'd asked whether the bureau was in a position to assist him or not; that's just not a concern in the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I will move on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning the state security directorate, and that is something you mentioned in your report, you said that it is under supervision of the parliament. How does that supervision operate when it comes to this part of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The supervision over this part of the Ministry of the Interior is carried out by the assembly, by the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, through a standing parliamentary committee that has the competence to control the work of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is the parliamentary commission comprised of, of who in particular?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This parliamentary committee comprised representatives of all parliamentary groups in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, and, as a rule, this committee is chaired by an MP from the largest opposition party.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning that and given there are different political parties in the parliament, can you tell me whether there is an ethnic key in terms of the composition of that commission and the composition of the parliament?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Of course, because I said members of all parliamentary groups are represented and they could come from various ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just before that leave that and to assist me, Ms. Residovic, perhaps the professor could tell me, then, what is the relationship between this parliamentary committee and Article 14 of the Law on Internal Affairs which you have open in front of you, I think, still on the screen, which says that the director reports his work to the minister.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is actually part of the horizontal mutual control between various pillars of government of power in the Republic of Macedonia. The parliament, as the legislative branch of power exercises the control over the government as the executive branch of power and that can be seen very well from the operation of the standing committee, standing parliamentary committee, that controls the work of the state security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand clearly now, I think, what you're saying. You were not suggesting that only the parliamentary committee has any control over the work of the directorate; the director is also obliged to report to the minister within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The director is answerable to the minister, and of course he also reports to the government of the Republic of Macedonia, which is the organ appointing the director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, while the parliamentary committee exercises control over the directorate -- of the work of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence as an independent body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm sorry for interfering.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour, in clarifying this. Could I ask that we go back to the previous issue as I believe it may be of some importance. I will have another question of Professor. This issue has to do with the use of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence in investigating a crime. That question was also asked of witness Sofija Galeva at page 8798, in line 8. The question was -- [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel should continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I received no interpretation. If members of the UBK sector for counter-intelligence and security are supposed to identify policemen who participated in the operation, the members of the UBK could come by information, could they not? And we received an open-ended answer of the witness, because she said that it would be but one of the ways. Would this be sufficient basis for me to ask two additional questions to the witness, in relation to some previous questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't see, but I'm prepared to allow you because you see, and you know what you want. I don't. So go ahead, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, let us go back to some of my previous questions when you talked about the specific methods and means at the disposal of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence. In your experience and knowledge, is the directorate for counter-intelligence and security capable to conduct crime operations? That is, activities usually undertaken by --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Complete your question, please, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, and according to your experience, is the administration of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence capable of undertaking on-site investigations and pre-trial procedures which usually fall within the remit of the criminal police?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. The directorate for security and counter-intelligence does not have at its disposal the means necessary to carry out pre-investigation activities that fall within the remit of crime police, so it could not perform these activities, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, did you now have a point?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I thought I did, Your Honour, but I thought better of it. So, no, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, let us move on to another topic you provided your conclusions an opinion on in the report that was forwarded to the Defence and to the Chamber. I have a few general questions and I'm seeking to find out some general answers from you about the issue of disciplinary procedure. First of all, can you tell us this: According to your knowledge of the laws and regulations of the Republic of Macedonia, who can a disciplinary procedure be instituted against within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Within the Ministry of the Interior, as well as within other organs in the state, the disciplinary procedure can be instigated against the employees of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, are internal affairs tasks performed only by the employees of the Ministry of Interior or are there other persons which, at times, can perform such tasks?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In -- it is usual that the activities of internal affairs are carried out by the employees of the Ministry of the Interior. However, there are situations that are provided for in the Law on Internal Affairs when other individuals could be retained to -- or deployed to perform such activities and there are also situations when reserve forces could be called up and even students from the police academy who could be involved in the performance of specific tasks under specific circumstances that are stipulated in the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, are elected officials employees of the Ministry of the Interior; namely, the minister and his deputy?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The minister and the deputy minister are not employees with the Ministry of Interior. They are employed with the government of the Republic of Macedonia and they do not fall under the disciplinary responsibility concept within the Ministry of Interior, since the principle of political responsibility applies to them and they are accountable and responsible before the government and the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia for the performance of their competencies within the laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note the time, Your Honours. Perhaps this would be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. We will have the first break now and resume in half an hour, at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before continuing with the questions, I kindly ask the usher to distribute the second document binder. As you can see, this one contains the footnotes that the professor provided and also indicates the references she used.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, in paragraphs 42 to 44 on page 12 of your report, you spoke about the employees of the Ministry of the Interior. That would be the issue that we started discussing before the break. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And also in this part you included your references in the footnotes, the references on the basis of which, in addition to your academic and professional knowledge and experience, you drew your conclusions in this report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. In this part of the report, specifically in addition to the Law on Internal Affairs, I used the labour law, the collective agreement of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I kindly ask that the witness be shown the Exhibit P86. That is the Law on Internal Affairs, Article 48. The Macedonian page is N000-8991; and the English page is N000-8973. Madam Professor, tell me whether this was the provision of the Law on Internal Affairs that you had in mind when making your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This is Article 48, which pertains to labour relations and establishing employment in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether there were any modifications with regards to these general terms under which an employment would commence, in the period 2001/2002?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In regards to this Article there was an amendment which was based on the decision of the constitutional court of the Republic of Macedonia, this being that paragraph 1 and 2 of this Article should be stricken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that the Law on Labour and Employment was also a ground for your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, the labour law, the general law which applies for all other employees also in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask that the witness now be shown Exhibit P553, Article 14, which is in page N000-2 -- N002-5380. That is the page in Macedonian language. And the English is N006-3827; that would be the fifth page out of the 40. As you stated already, Professor Taseva, that is the general law that applies to any and every employee, so also including the employees with the Ministry of the Interior, and this Article states that the employment commences when an employment contract is signed between the employee and the employer. Tell me, was this the provision that you had in mind when drawing your conclusion and when you were answering my question a moment ago, that the employment commences when a contract, employment contract, is signed?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. In preparing my expert opinion, I had in mind this provision of the labour law that establishes that employment is concluded based on a contract agreement between the employer and the employee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this, would it be possible for someone to commence their employment without signing the employment contract?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Employment is concluded exclusively and is based exclusively with the signing of the contract between the employee and the employer. It is not possible to have such employment without a contract between the employer and the employee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Article 15 of this law that we are now reviewing, reads: "The employee cannot commence employment prior to the signing and the verification of the employment contract." Are you aware, Professor Taseva, whether this legal basis was consistently followed also in the acts of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This legal provision pertains to all persons who enter into employment in the Republic of Macedonia. The Ministry of the Interior is not an exception to this provision. This provision therefore pertains also to the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If there are any special conditions required to commence the employment, would it be necessary for the employee to meet these specific requirements as well in order for them to become an employee of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In view of the specific character of the competencies of the Ministry of Interior, persons who enter into employment in the Ministry of Interior should fulfil also some other conditions. Parts of these conditions are, for example, to go through certain training, to prepare for carrying out their duties and tasks once they enter into regular employment. That is to say, once they conclude a contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, once the employee has signed the employment contract and thus became the employee of the Ministry of Interior and then failed to meet those conditions that are stipulated in the law or in the collective agreement, what then happens with that employee? Is he still an employee or would something else happen, as provided in the rules?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: If the person with the work contract, with the work employment contract does not fulfil some of the specific conditions, such as, for example, the necessary training which this person must undergo in a given period of time and the passing of exams or tests, if the employee does not pass the foreseen -- the exams or tests foreseen for this specific contract, then the contract is severed. He can no longer remain in employment of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once the employment contract is signed with the Ministry of the Interior, are there any consequences derived from that contract, consequences to the employee, actually, are there certain rights and obligations that begin entering into force?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Of course after the employment contract is signed, the employee gains all rights of employment, but also he is obliged to perform all obligations that stem from this employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the employee does not carry out his duties properly, tell me, Professor Taseva, is there any way establish the responsibility of that officer?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The manner or calling someone to responsibility of the employees who overstep their obligations or fail to fulfil their obligation is the disciplinary proceeding. Therefore this proceeding is one of the ways in which a person can be called to responsibility for failure to fulfill their obligations which are part of their employment. In the case of the Ministry of Interior, there is also a collective agreement which is concluded between the employer and representatives of the employees, and this collective agreement strictly regulates the conditions and cases under which a disciplinary proceeding can be led under an employee of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Professor Taseva, answering one of my questions in terms of who can perform the tasks in the area of internal affairs, you mentioned the reservists as well. And then you only indicated such possibility, while in your report, on page 13, in paragraphs -- from 45 to 50, you provided your opinion and presented also certain conclusions with regards to the position of the reservists within the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And this is in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you, Professor Taseva, tell us what are the duties that the minister of the interior has in relation to the reserve forces of the police?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs, the minister of the interior can, under certain conditions prescribed by law, reach a decision to include other persons other than those employed in the ministry with the aim of securing certain security conditions. Under such conditions, the minister has the competence to order a call-up of the reserve forces of the police forces and to include these forces in the work tasks, together with the regular force of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any regulation or legal act on the basis of which the call-up of the reserve forces is carried out; and if there is such act, who is then bringing it?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The act for call-up of the reserve forces in the Ministry of Interior is passed by the minister of the interior on the basis of the Law of Internal Affairs, and this falls under the competencies of the minister. That is to say, one of his competencies of passing by-laws which are under his competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And once the reservists are called up and they respond to the request to perform their duties for the Ministry of the Interior, do they, by this token, become employees of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Members of the reserve forces, in this case we're talking about the reserve force of the Ministry of Interior, but we can also speak about the other parts of the reserve forces, because they are also there in the army, they're not employees in -- of the Ministry of Interior. These are people who are employed elsewhere. They have regular employment at a different place, whether it be in an institution or in the private sector. What is important is that they have deployment as reserve forces of the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia and that, according to this deployment, they are assigned as part of the reserve forces of the Ministry of Interior. As such, therefore, they're called up to carry out some of the competencies and functions of the Ministry of Interior, but they're not employees of the ministry. The minister passes a particular act in regards to them, which regulates the remuneration for the period when they were engaged to carry out these tasks. However, they do not become employees; they're not persons employed in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us just now that the minister passes a special act, a decision or another act by which the remuneration of the reservists for their activities is established. Just tell me, could they be subject to a disciplinary procedure within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. They cannot be subject to disciplinary proceeding, in view of the fact that they did not have the status of employees of the ministry. We already mentioned that only employees can be subject to disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a person is called up to the reserve force, what are the duties where that individual is deployed? Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: When a person is called to the reserve force of the Ministry of Interior, he can be assigned to several and almost all, I would say, tasks carried out by the ministry, be it in uniform, in the police, or be it in another workplace, in everything which is foreseen in the plans for deployment of the reserve forces regarding the needs and the intent of their call-up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, on the basis of the regulation that you’re aware of and also on the basis of your experience, those reservists that are deployed to certain posts, to whom are they answerable?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I previously said that they are deployed to carry out part of the competencies of the Ministry of Interior together with the regular employees of the ministry. They are therefore directly answerable for their work to the superior to which they are assigned to carry out their tasks. This can be anyone, any superior, at any rank or level in the ministry, where these persons, as members of the reserve forces, are assigned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And tell us, if this member of the reserve forces would perpetrate a criminal offence, what would be the way, then, for them to be taken to responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: As all citizens in the Republic of Macedonia who would perpetrate a criminal offence, a procedure would be led for establishing the existence of a criminal offence, much as is in the case of all other citizens.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On page 14 of your report, in item 51, you spoke of the contractual relations between certain individuals and the minister. Tell me, what would this be?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Paragraph 51 in fact served me to explain a situation which can happen in the Ministry of Interior or in other places that there are other relationships related to work tasks, be it by a contract for deed or other type of contracts for carrying out engagements. In this case, these are persons who the Ministry of Interior and other institutions could engage for a concrete task, which is related to the daily work of the Ministry of Interior. For example, a practice as of a few years ago is that the premises of the Ministry of Interior are cleaned by private companies with whom the ministry has a contract. Contracts who work on maintenance of the facilities. Further, this can be services for translation. In the case of meetings, we have need for interpretation and for these purposes we conclude agreements, contracts with companies who have and offer these kind of services.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, what would be the nature of such contract? You gave us example of two cases. What would be the legal nature of that contract between the ministry and an individual or an organisation?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: These are typical contractual obligations, an agreement; this is not an employer-employee relationship. This is a civil relationship, contractual relationship.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if such party to the contract fails to perform its obligation, what would be the way to resolve that problem?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In the case that one of the parties, anyone, failed to meet these obligations, the courts are responsible and they're listed in the contracts as competent in the case of disputes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, in paragraphs 52 to 55, you spoke about the concept of authorised official. That is on pages 14 and 15 of your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This part of the report pertains to the concept of authorised officials in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, with regards to this concept that you spoke of in paragraphs 52, 53, 54, and 55, is there equal status between an employee of the minister and authorised official? Tell me, would this be -- in some way be the identical notion or are there any differences between the two notions?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: One cannot say that this is an identical term, because there are certain differences. Not all authorised officials are employees of the Ministry of Interior, and also not all employees of the Ministry of Interior are authorised officials. There are both categories of persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, Madam Professor, what would be an example of that, when some employee would be an employee but not an authorised official; and the opposite situation, when an individual could be an authorised official without being an employee with the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In the Ministry of Interior, there are a number of categories of employees. Some of these categories - and in item 53, I list these categories - that persons who work in the police and operative activities, they're authorised officials. Persons who carry out activities that are in direct connection with the police and operative activities also have the status of authorised officials. However, all others who carry out other tasks and work duties and who are no -- have no connection with the police and operative work, do not have the status of authorised officials. These are civil servants who are employed in the Ministry of Interior. A typical example of a case when someone is not employed in the ministry but can be authorised is the status of the minister of the interior and his deputy for whom, as I previously said, they're not employed at the Ministry of the Interior because they're employed at the government, and the Law on Internal Affairs gives them the authorisations and considers them as authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we spoke about the reserve forces in the ministry a moment ago, you stated that they were not employees in the ministry. With regards to this concept of authorised official, tell me, do they have the rights and the authorisations that an authorised official would have?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Considering the tasks that they need to perform, the members of the reserve forces, during the time when they're active within the units or the services, parts of the Ministry of the Interior, they do have the status of authorised official, but that is -- does not entail employment status. It is only linked to the activity or the task that they're entrusted with at the moment during that period when they are activated as members of the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answering my previous question, you referred to paragraph 53. Therein, you enumerate the categories of persons who enjoy the status of authorised officials. Professor, tell me, what are the reasons for these categories of persons enjoy the status of authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The main reason why the law or the legislature has given a special status to this category of individuals is based on their competencies and the functions they need to perform within the Ministry of the Interior. The work of the police, for the most part, consists -- they are uniformed officers of the Ministry of Interior who are carrying weapons and who are applying special measures in order to perform their working duties. Also, the employees in the operative police or the operative workers, as they are called, operatives as they are called in the Law on Internal Affairs are also employees that -- or individuals that within their everyday duties have the duty to apply special measures, such as would be measures to investigate crimes, surpress crime, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you for a moment, Professor Taseva. In paragraph 53, you state that the minister, and you cited the law, that the minister, his deputy and other managing personnel enjoy the status of authorised officials. Does this mean that the minister has the powers and obligation to perform all tasks, or, rather, to use all authority envisaged by the law and other regulation of the ministry pertaining to authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. That does not mean that at all. Since the minister of the interior is an official office holder, he is an employee of the government and the competencies and that the minister and the deputy are entrusted with are primarily functional competencies. The purpose of which is to enable the minister to perform his role and function as a head and a manager of the Ministry of the Interior, but at the same time, to perform his legal duties pursuant to other legislative items as a member of the government of the Republic of Macedonia. As a minister of the interior, he needs to enact regulation that governs the work of the ministry and that establishes the ways in which the authorised officials will act. Also the Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Organisation of MOI also provide many competences that the minister of the interior needs to carry out as the office holder who is the head of the ministry. So the competences of the authorities are mainly functional, not operative competences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the word "operative function". The minister, given his position within the legal system of the Republic of Macedonia, and, in particular, within the Ministry of the Interior, is he the person who performs the tasks envisaged in Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. The minister does not perform operative or operational tasks as provided by Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs. That is performed by the employees in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the minister ever perform a task of an operative nature, and if such a possibility exists, who can provide such authority to him to carry out certain tasks of an operative nature?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Certain tasks that one would call tasks of operative nature are provided for the minister in other acts, acts on organisation of the government. In the Law on Internal Affairs, for instance, there is a provision saying that the minister can order undertaking of certain operative measures. But those are only specific cases that are enumerated in the law. Another case might be when the minister would need to follow a decision or a conclusion of the government, which actually contains the provisions where the minister is requested to undertake certain activities in order to meet the operative demands or issues that are derived from the competencies of the minister stipulated in the Law on Internal Affairs. And in some cases, that could also be the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the minister have any operative powers when it comes to investigating, detecting and identifying crimes and perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I said already, the minister is the office holder, a politician, who is appointed to head the Ministry of the Interior. He is not an employee with the Ministry of the Interior who would have the obligation and competencies to perform part of these operative functions of the Ministry of the Interior. That would mean that the minister of the interior could not undertake such actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Explaining this, you also said that in exceptional circumstances the law can authorise the minister to undertake operative measures, partly or in whole.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that the witness be shown P86, Article 30. It is N000-8986 in the Macedonian; and N000-8969 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you have that provision of Article 30 before you. In the first paragraph what is mentioned is a measure of sealing off a building in order to apprehend perpetrators. In paragraph 2, it is stated that the minister, or person authorised by him, can order undertaking the measures envisaged in paragraph 1 of this Article. When you said a moment ago that in exceptional circumstances the minister can undertake a measure which may be deemed operative in nature, would this be one of such measures that you had in mind, when you came to that conclusion or opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. This is a provision which incorporates this type of competences of the Ministry of Interior and it expressly states that, in order to prevent crimes, detect and apprehend perpetrators of crime or to secure facilities, the authorised officials can close the access to a certain open area or to prevent individuals from leaving that area. These measures are performance of official tasks and they can be ordered by a minister or an officer authorised by them. Since it is a specific measure which in some way interferes with the constitutional liberties of freedom of movement of the citizens, the legislature has provided that this specific competence would belong to the minister of the interior as the office holder who is the head of the ministry, or to an officer authorised by the minister. I said this is one of the possibilities that are incorporated in the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given your professional experience, Professor Taseva, does the minister make use of this original authority under law, or is it more frequent that the minister delegates that authority to another person as envisaged by the Article?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: As far as I know, also from my personal practice from when I worked in the Ministry of the Interior, is that usually this type of measures are undertaken by individuals who are authorised by the minister of the interior. Or let me be more precise. I'm not aware of a single case where the minister of the interior would order that such type of measures are ordered. Usually those are persons who are authorised by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When testifying about the fact that the minister can, on occasion, have operative powers, you mentioned the law, a decision by the government, or by the president. Do you still stand by that, and is that corroborated by the situation described in the Article?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Law on Internal Affairs and the rule books you mentioned in your footnotes, a number, a great number of powers or authorities are mentioned pertaining to those enjoyed by authorised officials. Can any authorised official perform all of those authorities; and, if not, how is it ascertained that the given person performs the relevant tasks and authorities?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The competencies or authorisations that belong to the employees in the Ministry of the Interior are basically many measures and means that they can employ in the course of their work, but it does not mean in any way that every employee of the minister who is an authorised official could employ all measures that within this sphere of authorisations. What measures can be used by which of the employees in the course of their work depends on the tasks and duties that this post entails and that is described in the act for systematization for the work and job positions in the Ministry of the Interior. That would mean that every duty or every job posts has specific authorisations and obligations and the holders of those posts, those employees can use those specific authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, is it possible, under the law, and does it exist in practice that an authorised official or with a certain scope of authority of authorised official can go and do, perform other tasks which do not fall under that person's authority but such authority is envisaged by the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
