utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I should best use my own example, I think, because I, as the director of the police academy am an authorised official. I have the authorisation, I have the ID card that every employee of the ministry has, but I cannot apply any of the measures that belong to this group of measures applied by the authorised officials of the Ministry of the Interior. For instance, I can't go to the street and regulate the traffic. I can't ask the persons to identify themselves through an ID. I can't really do any other action. I can't detain a person, because those do not belong to the domain of my working duties. It is precisely stipulated in the laws and the by-laws of the ministry which are the obligations that each post entails and which are the authorisations that can be used by the person performing these competences.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, line 47:4, instead of laws, acts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned your example illustrating this. But, for example, does an outpatient clinic or a physician exist within the Ministry of the Interior, and do people employed there enjoy the status of authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. That would be another good illustration of the notion of authorised official who could not use specific authorisations. Within the police, there is an outpatient institution. The doctor is an authorised official but they could not use all the measures. They could use only those that are specified for his or her specific post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Going back to your own example, you said that you cannot apprehend or detain a person for 24 hours. Concerning that answer of yours, I want to refer to Article 29 of the Law on Internal Affairs. That is P86, which states that the authorised officials of the ministry have the right to detain someone for the maximum of 24 hours. From your answer I gather that you, although you are an authorised official cannot exercise that right. You cannot do that, did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I don't have such right and I cannot exercise that right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And nor can your physician?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: No. Our police physician, physician from the police academy can't do that as well. We can use other examples. For instance, if there is a theft within the police academy, apart from the director there are other authorised officials there but in such case, we still address the nearest police station and we request that the measures for detection of a perpetrator of the crime are undertaken by them. We ourselves can't undertake activities in terms of detection of a perpetrator of a crime that has been perpetrated within the premises of the police academy because this falls outside of our competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor, while we are on the topic of detecting and investigating crimes and the competencies of an authorised official, who are actually the persons and relevant bodies within the Ministry of the Interior who have the authority to work on the tasks of determining, first of all, whether an event represents a crime, and then, secondly, on identifying the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Registering the event, detecting that a crime has been perpetrated or what activities were perpetrated within that crime and also undertaking measures to detect the perpetrators of such crime are activities that are carried out at the level of basic units of the Ministry of the Interior. Those would be the police stations, OVRs and then further up it could be at the level of SVR, depending on the location where certain activity has taken place. I told you a while ago that with regards to an event within the premises of the police academy we would address the nearest police station which covers the area where the police academy has its premises.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please show P88 to the expert. It is the Law on Criminal Procedure, Article 140 of the law. In the Macedonian it is N001-9056; and in the English version, it is 32 of 182, and page 33 of 182. ERN is N001-9208. Professor, in Article 140, paragraph 1 it states that: The state bodies and institutions performing public competencies have the duty to report crimes that are prosecuted ex officio, regarding which they were informed or of which they learned in a different manner. Professor Taseva, can you tell me which state bodies are those foreseen by this regulation?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Those are all state bodies and all institutions in the state that perform public competences. They're not enumerated. All state bodies, all institutions performing public competences have the duty to report crimes that are prosecuted ex officio.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you're trying to say that this includes the Ministry of Interior as one of the state bodies.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Naturally. The Ministry of the Interior as a state body, is one of them. Also is the Ministry of Finance as a state body, the police academy as well, as a state body. All state institutions have the duty to report crimes prosecuted ex officio.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among those organs, are there any parts which execute such tasks, and if so, how is it ascertained who is to bear responsibility when it comes to this part of obligations?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Within the internal structure of the state organs there are organisational parts that are tasked with this part of competencies. Some of the state bodies, such as, for instance, the ministry of finance, have within them several bodies. Those would be the customs administration, the public revenue office, the financial police, the directorate for prevention of money laundering. All those bodies have legal competencies and duties to detect and report criminal offences, but within the ministry of finance, for instance, there are other services such as various inspectorates. Supervision bodies that also have competences in terms of filing criminal reports. So depending on the type of competence within the bodies, there are parts specialised. Namely identified are the services who are tasked with performing such duties and that is specifically provided for each of the state bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, if you want to answer the question, who within the state body or institution is responsible for the execution of this legal obligation, then one needs to go to the various by-laws and other regulation of that body.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is so. You understand me well. One needs to look at the internal organisational structure, the act for the organisational of the work of that particular work body. The act of systematization of workplaces will further show the duties and tasks of those involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to what you said I conclude concerning the position of the Ministry of the Interior within the state administration that the Ministry of the Interior is but one of such organs. Within the Ministry of Interior, which are its organs that are authorised to submit criminal reports once they ascertained that there is a crime that had been committed and that they have to prosecute ex officio?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: As part of the internal organisation and structure of the Ministry of Interior, proceedings regarding the uncovering or reporting or submitting a criminal report is always part of the basic units of the Ministry of the Interior, the so-called police stations, or units of internal affairs, OVRs, because it -- they pertain to the place where this crime has been committed, taking activities to uncover it and submitting the relevant criminal reports to the public prosecutor and the courts. In the case of a complex or more specific case, then more than one, several police units or several OVRs within a sector act together, and depending on the competencies where most of the persons involved in this complex persons are located or the place where this crime has happened, then the criminal report can be sent on the level of OVR or even at the higher joint level of SVR. And depending on the complexity of the case, it can even be done so that a criminal report be submitted by the Ministry of Interior itself which is extremely rare.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answering my question, you raised a number of other issues, and I will ask you for some clarification. Namely, when explaining who can submit a criminal report, first, you mentioned territorial jurisdiction. Professor, when it comes to investigating crimes and prosecuting perpetrators, is territorial jurisdiction of importance, and what is the conduct of all organs which have to do with investigating crimes when it comes to territorial jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Territorial jurisdiction is important both from the point of view of the procedure for uncovering and detecting the perpetrators plus also later on for leading the criminal procedures within the judicial bodies. So this territorial jurisdiction where this crime has been perpetrated and where the perpetrator was found are very important in terms of how the procedure for establishing the circumstances for detecting the perpetrators and initiating the criminal procedure will be led.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand the competences of the police stations and OVRs as well when it comes to investigating crimes and prosecuting perpetrators, it is closely related to the issue of territorial jurisdiction. As you say, such people, such bodies are there in the place where the crime has been committed. What is their role to shed light on any given event and what is their role in catching the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is of importance for the overall procedure, for informing the competent judicial bodies, for informing the competent public prosecutor. We always say 'the competent investigating judge' and 'the competent public prosecutor'. This stems from jurisdiction, depending on the territory and where –- on the territory of which public prosecutor or of which Court we are in. They also denote the territory where the prior activities will be taken for uncovering and detecting the perpetrators of that crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with your professional experience and also when reviewing the material forwarded to you by this Defence, did you base your conclusion that the organs found at the base of the Ministry of the Interior are those competent to perform such tasks and does it all confirm what you have just said before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. The materials, the manner of systematization and structuring of the Ministry of Interior and those who act within the Ministry of Interior is in fact the manner which I have just now explained before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Such organs found at the lowest level of the ministry, that is the OVRs, do they have competent personnel to do so, and is the ministry organised in such a way that such personnel is positioned well, geographically speaking, to be able to investigate crimes and detect perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: We could talk about this depending on the criminal act in question, about the crime in question. In cases where we have a more complex crime that requires more specific operative measures such as, for example, even the on-site investigation by criminalistic and ballistic -- police forensic expertise, if it needs to suppress criminal acts such as separating organised groups for -- for trade in human beings it can be that the uncovering of perpetrators of crime can happen in coordination in close correlation between several bodies of internal affairs or by a direct link with the structures at the Ministry of Interior by chain of command towards the centre in the Ministry of Interior. If I have not been clear enough, for example, let's say we have a case that has happened on the territory of a number of police stations. This then will be coordinated by the sector of internal affairs. If measures and -- coordinated and complex measure needs to be taken to uncover this event, coordination can be done at a higher level because at a lower level the people do not have the necessary operative and technical measures which they require to clarify this case. However, they may also not have the necessary knowledge or qualifications to that end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, when you mentioned the competencies of the sectors of the Ministry of Interior in your report, and then the Ministry of Interior, in particular the directorate of public security you put particular stress on the coordination role of those organs. When talking about identifying perpetrators and investigating crimes and having in mind what you just said, to what extent is territorial jurisdiction combined with the other aspects of work of the bodies of the Ministry of Interior, in case such competencies fall outside the remit and jurisdiction of any given OVR?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In case when an event, a crime, has happened outside the territory of a police station or a given OVR, then it is always the higher levels that become involved in uncovering and resolving the crime, which means that in addition to departments of the interior sectors of the interior get involved according to hierarchy. If it is an organised criminal group which operates on the entire territory of the state, then all these activities are coordinated by the central services at the Ministry of the Interior. And in such a case the jurisdiction is determined by the location where the majority of the crimes have been committed or where the majority of the perpetrators –- are to be found. If it is a more complex crime that encompasses the overall territory of the state it is referred to the highest level, to the central level, where the criminal report or act is submitted. That will result in a more 15 coordinated work of the judicial bodies at the level of the State Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, if I understood what you said well, the basic principle of territorial jurisdiction ... Is it combined with the other principle of coordination as a higher type of organisation, higher order type of organisation of the Ministry of Interior? Is that the way you clarify it, the roles of OVRs, SVRs and the ministry itself in the report?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. It is combined in this way, and it is connected to the principle of efficiency and effectiveness. Everything is coordinated at the level of the MOI and is later implemented in a way that will ensure the greatest efficiency and effectiveness in clarifying a certain event.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In practice, Madam Professor, which are the bodies, which for the main part submit criminal reports? At what level of the ministry are those persons or bodies?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The practice, criminal reports, for the most part are filed at the lowest level. These are the police stations, that is to say, the OVRs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said that in case crime base covers the entirety territory of a republic and that detecting such crimes can go up to the highest professional level of the ministry, can you tell us what is that highest professional level that can submit a criminal report in such a case?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In such a case -- we said if there is such a case, then this would be the highest superior at the directorate for public security, and this would be its director.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the second break now and resume at five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would mention that, unfortunately, Judge Van den Wyngaert is unable to continue sitting today. I'd expect that she will be sitting again in the morning, or in the afternoon tomorrow, and Judge Thelin and I will sit this last session under the Rule. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I just mention that my comments at the beginning may be fading in your recollection, certain things seem to have been laboured a little more than need be. A gentle reminder, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will bear your instruction in mind. However I do think that I cut short but at least one third concerning my questions, although it is very difficult to achieve, given that I had a concept of my examination-in-chief. However, I will do my utmost to meet your request. If I forget that occasionally, that is simply due to this ideal concept that I had envisaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, I believe together we can meet His Honour's request, and I apologise yet again for having failed to meet it in full. Before the break, we were talking about the most senior level within the ministry structure, at which supposing the conditions you described were in place could submit a criminal report. Do you remember discussing that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, you mentioned the various directors within the Ministry of the Interior. Do you recall that? It is at page 18, paragraphs 71, 72, 73, and 74, as well as 75. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To backtrack a bit, can you tell me who appoints directors and under what procedure, when we talk about individual organs within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The directors of the bodies within the Ministry of Interior, the director of the bureau for public security, and the director of the direction for security and counter-intelligence are appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how do they go about performing their function within the organ to which they had been appointed as directors?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we have bodies within the Ministry of Interior, both directors appointed by the government perform their functions independently leading the sectors which they're charged with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that, tell me whether the directors of organs that are part of the Ministry of the Interior -- or, rather, can those directors be subject to disciplinary procedures?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the directors are appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia, they cannot be subject to a disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Should the directors fail to execute their tasks, who can raise the issue of responsibility and how?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In the case that the directors fail to carry out their tasks and duties, and in view of the fact that they're accountable for their work before the minister and the government of the Republic of Macedonia, they can be dismissed from their office by the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor Taseva, previously you said that the minister and his deputy are not employees of the Ministry of the Interior and that they carry political responsibility. If the situation within their domain of activity is unfavorable they can be held accountable. Do you remember talking about that issue before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who can raise the issue of responsibility of the minister?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The issue of responsibility of the minister can be raised by the minister [as interpreted]. He can ask for the dismissal and removal of the minister but this can also be done by the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I did not understand well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You seem to have said that the minister can raise the issue of responsibility or accountability of the minister. Is this a mistake? Did you misspeak? You said members of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I said the prime minister, not the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps it's a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is clear now. Thank you. When talking about the competences within the Ministry of the Interior, you said that the minister cannot influence daily -- the daily tasks of directors. Can the minister exert any influence on how the directors go about executing their tasks, daily, since you said that they are independent within their respective domains and should act according to the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The minister cannot influence in the performance of the everyday tasks of the directors of the directorate for public security and the directorate for security and counter-intelligence. Within the framework of carrying out their tasks, they act in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs and other laws which are under their competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, we already discussed several important issues regarding the position the minister enjoys within the Ministry of the Interior. I have a few others on top of that. Is it correct that, concerning the role and position of the minister within the Ministry of the Interior, you gave your opinion and findings in paragraph 56 to paragraph 69, pages 15 through to 18?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. This part of the report pertains to the role and position of the minister in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your findings in the report, you said that the minister enjoys the competencies prescribed by the law. Tell me, can the minister assign certain authority to himself, which does not stem from the law or any governmental or presidential decision, since those two bodies can assign competencies to him?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This cannot be done by any minister and consequently not by the minister of the interior. The minister cannot bestow authorisations upon themselves or undertake measures which are not provided for by the law, be it by the Law on Internal Affairs or the Law on the Government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order to make it even clearer for me, I wanted to put a hypothesis to you. Let's say that the person in charge of the sector in the city of Skopje does not act in accordance with the law and regulations in performing his tasks, and the director of the directorate of public security does -- is not carrying out his obligations pertaining to the implementation of laws, can the minister, maybe to use an unfortunate term, assume the position, take their role in performing those tasks?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is not possible. The minister cannot undertake the authorisations and competencies of other senior positions in the ministry, even of any employee in the ministry. If they do not or if they fail to carry out their competencies, there are other measures that can be taken, but the minister cannot sit in their place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Answering to my previous question you said that the minister of the interior, including other ministers, cannot do anything that is not envisaged by the law. Professor Taseva, what is the basic law, piece of legislation regulating the competencies of all ministries, since you said neither the interior minister nor the other ministers?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is, above all, the Law on the Organisation and Work of Government Institutions and the Law on Government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show Exhibit P92 to the witness. That is the Law on Organisation and Work of the State Administration Bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, do the regulations contained in this law obligate all of the ministers, including the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The provisions of this law are obligatory for the minister of the interior and all bodies which are covered by this law, the bodies of the government administration, which includes also the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Should a provision of the law in respect of an individual ministry, say, the Ministry of the Interior, be in contrast or in contravention of this law, is there such a provision foreseeing that the Law on Organisation and Work of State Body Institutions exist?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this is a systemic law, the provisions of this Law on the Organisation and Work of the Bodies of State Administration will have priority over the provisions of the Law on Internal Affairs as a special law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If this particular law establishes that in a ministry, such as the Ministry of Interior, there are organs within the ministry, would such a regulation be put into force immediately, even though it is not contained in the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this law regulates that there are two bodies within the Ministry of Interior, this law is applied and two bodies are set up within the ministry, even though this is not foreseen in the Law of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: An overall review of all documents and regulation that you saw ... Can you tell us whether in 2000 and 2001, as part of the ministry, there existed such two organs which, independently, carried out their tasks within their respective domains?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after this Law on Organisation and Work of the Bodies of State Administration was adopted, and it established that there would be two bodies within the Ministry of the Interior, so in addition to the directorate for security and counter-intelligence that was also provided by the Law on Internal Affairs, this law establishes also the bureau of public security as a body within the Ministry of the Interior. Immediately after that, the implementation of this law was provided for. This body within the Ministry of Interior was established, the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please show Article 55 of the law to the witness. It is at N001-9805 in the Macedonian; and in the English version, it is N001-9490-N001-9511-ET. Madam Professor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please. The microphone of the counsel is off again. The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to start over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think I'm the culprit, Ms. Residovic. One of my papers was touching a switch that have I here. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, the Article reads: "The minister enacts rules, orders, guidelines, plans, programmes, decisions, and other types of acts for the execution of laws and other regulations, when he is authorised to do so by law." When talking about the authorities of the minister being stipulated in the law, is this the -- is this Article one of the basis you used to come up with your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes. This law that is as you stated the systemic and the umbrella law, in a way, pertains to all ministers. When it speaks about the minister, it speaks about any minister in the government of the Republic of Macedonia. And it provides that the minister or the ministers enact rule books, orders and any other act necessary for the operation of the ministries that they're heads of, but those are situations when they enact those things, when they are authorised to do so by the law. So these authorisations are incorporated in other special laws. For instance, the Law on Internal Affairs mentions several times that the minister needs to enact a document that falls within the remit and this is also the basic competence derived from this law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with your answer, if I were to say that the minister has the authority delegated to him or contained in the law, would that be in accordance with your conclusion, stated in your report and before this trial?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at Article 49 and one of its provisions. My question concerns your opinion that this law needs to be implemented prior to any other specific law being implemented. Article 49, does it pertain to any specific minister; or, does it set out the role of all ministers?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This Article, Article 49, applies to all ministers in the government of the Republic of Macedonia. When it says "a minister," it refers to all ministers in the government, or any minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If this Article states that: "The minister represents the ministry," would some lexis specialis, so a special law governing a given area, be able to decide that the ministry is represented differently, other than the provision contained in this law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This could not be done differently from what this law provides. Usually in the legal practice in the Republic of Macedonia the provisions of the systemic laws are transposed in the provisions of the specific laws, and when it is not done, then the provisions of the general, of the systemic laws are applicable.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, does the same apply to the ability of the minister to issue orders? Is that authority the same for all ministers; or, is there a different situation when it comes to the minister of the interior? I refer you to Article 55 of the law.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The possibility to issue orders belongs to other ministers as well. That is not a specific situation for one of the minister only. All ministers within the performance of their duties can issue orders that are lawful and that are related to the performance of the competencies within the remit of the ministry that they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When can any minister, including the minister of the interior, issue orders?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: When there is a basis for that in the law and when it is related to enforcing certain decisions of the government or of the parliament, and which are related to the execution of the role of the ministry that they're heads of.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, concerning this law for which you say is a systemic or umbrella law pertaining to all ministers and not individual ministers, tell me whether the legal position of the minister -- of the ministers, is the same; or, is there a distinction between them when it comes to their powers stemming from the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: There is nothing that would make one minister different from another, when it comes to exercising their options and competencies having in mind the spirit of this law. In the performance of their options, all ministers in all ministries in the government are equal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the difference, then, between the ministries and ministers? What's the difference between the minister of the interior from the minister of culture, for example?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The difference is actually stemming out of the competencies that the ministries have, the ministries that they're heads of. The ministries themselves have different spheres of competencies, but the ministers, as a rule, are political figures. They are politicians who have been appointed by the parliament to exercise certain role as ministers in the government of the Republic of Macedonia and there is no difference between them, other than the functions of the ministries that they're heads of.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, if such differences giving different powers to different ministers exist, do they have to be prescribed in the law as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Any difference or distinction with regards to performance of the ministers are incorporated or stipulated in the laws that cover the respective area that the ministry covers. There is a law on education; there is a law on science; there is law on agriculture, on finance, on internal affairs. All of these laws specify the specific competencies of the ministers who are heading those ministries. So all of that is incorporated in the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony so far, you mentioned something and together we looked at Article 30, paragraph 2 of the Law on Internal Affairs, whereby the minister can order the sealing off of a building in order to apprehend perpetrators. Is that something which would be specific in the case of the minister of the interior or can something like that exist in the case of the minister of culture as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: That is a specific competence or authority vested in the minister of the interior. No other minister could perform such competencies. They are not vested with such competencies. No other minister is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Professor, let us look at paragraph 71 of your report, page 18. You state decisively when mentioning the function of directors that they are independent in exercising their duty. Why is such position stipulated when it comes to the various ministers within ministries?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The need to ensure maximum of professionalism in the performance of the office or the function that the Ministry of the Interior is to perform, and also, each of the bodies within the ministry as well. This is why these two bodies were established, and they have completely different competencies. To enable them to respond to their legal duties and obligations, these parts of the ministry, so these bodies within the ministry, have professionals as their heads and they are managing the bodies in terms of exercising the professional role and the competence of the ministry. In this case, this could be the bureau of public security or the directorate for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A little while ago you said that ministers are often political figures rather than professionals. Is that of any importance, given the fact that within the various organs of ministries there are professionals, career employees which perform tasks within the domain of the given ministry? Or in your view, it has no bearing on the composition of the various organs in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Within the state administration of the Republic of Macedonia efforts are made to distinguish between the professional and the political, or the politics. So as politicians, or as political office holders across all ministries, we have the minister and their deputy, whereas with regards to bodies within any of the ministries are headed by professionals who are competent to perform the competencies that this body, within the ministry, is entrusted with. In this case, Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, are you acquainted or do you know General Zoran Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is your opinion of him as a professional? Is he a capable professional, is he credible?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: He is a top professional. He is very capable, very credible, very competent in carrying out his obligations and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Testifying before this Court, General Zoran Jovanovski, clarifying the position of the Minister Boskoski and his attitude towards the -- or treatment of the professionals within the structure of the Ministry of the Interior, on page 5132, lines 23 and 24, General Jovanovski stated: "While Minister Boskoski was a minister," and I quote "the final word belonged to us, the professionals." Professor Taseva, does this testimony of General Jovanovski correspond to your understanding of the relation between the minister and his directors?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: It is very much in accordance of my understanding between the minister and his directors. I said myself that previously there is a delineation between the political and the professional, and the General in this regards is the professional.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And does it also correspond to your professional and academic knowledge that this is the legally provided situation that the directors of the bodies within the ministry are independent in the performance of their tasks and the minister could not exert influence over those bodies to prevent them from lawfully performing their duties?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the legal position. The positive legal position incorporated in the laws and the by-laws of the Republic of Macedonia, and the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you spoke about the situation when there would be crimes committed across a wider area within the Republic of Macedonia, that even the highest professional tier would be able to file a criminal report and when asked by me who would that highest professional tier be you said the director for public security. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, first of all, do you know of such cases and of how many such cases do you know from the practice?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: I personally do not know of any such case but I said that this is legally possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And with regards to the position of the minister, tell me, is the minister yet another professional tier in the ministry, or is he, as you testified before, a political figure chosen by the parliament?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In the case, the professional part of the ministry cannot extend to the minister which is to say that the minister cannot carry out these kind of tasks, he cannot file criminal reports. Therefore, he is the political segment of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And should the intention of the state that within the ministry the laws are carried out properly be not followed, what would be the minister's responsibility in case of such failure?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: If we're talking about the responsibility of the minister, once again, we're talking about politics and about political responsibility or accountability.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And also with regards to the position of the minister, who can be a minister, including the minister of the interior, who, or what kind of professionals could be ministers?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: The Law on the Organisation and Work of State Administration provides for an exception in the general provisions where it is stated that the ministers have to be experts in the areas of the portfolios that they will head. For example, the minister of culture has to know culture. The minister of health can be a manager or can be someone working in the medical professional. The law clearly states that the ministers of interior and the minister of Defence have to be civilians, persons who, in the least, two years prior to their appointment as ministers will be employed in a civil service -- in a civilian service. They will not be members of the -- member of the police forces or the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this just a legal provision or is it also a constitutional category?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: This is also a constitutional category. The constitution also stated that the portfolios of defence and police will be headed by civilians, by politicians. This is the result -- or it is due to the major authorisations which these ministries have and the intent of the constitutions and the laws which was to establish civilian control over these institutions which, in themselves, have components of arms and possibilities for other special measures in realising their work tasks and competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, considering the fact that the parliament chooses ministers, to the best of your knowledge, does the parliament respect this legal provision absolutely or have there been situations in the practice where there were certain deviations from this principle?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In practice, there have been situations of deviating from this principle, especially in the case of appointments of ministers of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, Minister Boskoski, before he was chosen to be minister, has for a number of years, two or three years, been an employee with the ministry. To what extent do you think that in his case there has been a significant deviation from this orientation of principle that you discussed just now?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA
utterances.text: In this case of Mr. Boskoski as well as in other cases which I am aware of - these are ministers before Mr. Boskoski as well as ministers that were appointed after him - for the most part, these are persons employed in the Ministry of Interior who belong to the so-called civilian structures. They were not uniformed persons. Due to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could be wrong, but I'm not aware where in the expert's report this whole line of questioning of the last five minutes is located, Your Honour, and where the basis for the witness's answers are. And it might be very difficult for the Prosecution to prepare its cross-examination on this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to point to any clear reference, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, apart from the chapter speaking about the position of the minister within the structure but also precisely the -- the precise position of the minister is not described in the report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the precise position of the minister as a civilian is not described in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Has that concluded your questioning on that point?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not get this answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. This concludes my examination with regards to this issue. Your Honours, considering that I have significantly reduced the number of questions that I have prepared for today, I could continue asking some -- about some matters from the report of Professor Taseva, but this would be in an inconsistent way. So if possible, I would prefer that I continue the examination of the professor tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you indicate how long you would expect to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is difficult for me to say it now because I need to significantly reduce the scope of this -- of my examination of this expert witness, because we previously indicated that the Defence will spend seven hours in examining this witness, and the Prosecutor, again, additional seven hours, but I believe that I will reduce this for at least an hour and a half or two hours. So less than planned time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now, but I would suggest that it ought to be possible to reduce even more than you are suggesting. It was the forecast that you would need seven hours when there was such a detailed and careful report that caused me to make the comments that I did make. So we leave it to your industry overnight, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. We must ask you to come back tomorrow when we continue sitting, which will be at 2.15. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
